comparison: Both evaluate the central findings about frequency modulation and chromatin-dependent transcriptional bursting (C2, C3, C22, C53, C66-C68). OpenEval finds these claims well-supported by converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers acknowledged technical novelty but expressed uncertainty about whether findings represent significant advances beyond prior knowledge of digital on-off states, requesting clarification of novelty.

Both address clonal variation and dose-response characteristics (C37-C40, C50-C51, C77). OpenEval finds the FISH data from multiple clonal lines strongly supports consistent EC50 and Hill coefficients. Peer reviewers expressed uncertainty about whether analyses were performed for each clonal line individually and whether the claimed parameter invariance across clones was actually demonstrated.

Both evaluate live-cell imaging data on transcriptional dynamics (C34-C35, C71-C73). OpenEval finds exponential distributions and dose-dependent off-times well-supported by quantitative data. Peer reviewers requested critical baseline control data (0 μM PA) and questioned whether analyses were performed for each clonal line, indicating uncertainty about completeness and generalizability.

Both address photoactivation experiments (C23, C61, C63, C65, C69-C70). OpenEval finds the single pulse/single burst observation well-supported with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers requested detailed statistical analyses of single vs. multiple cycles, questioned the mechanism of transient PA release, and asked for proof of the blocking mechanism by excess caged PA.

Both evaluate the experimental system design (C20-C21, C25-C26, C29-C32). OpenEval finds the MS2/FISH system well-characterized with appropriate technical details. Peer reviewers questioned fundamental aspects including whether there is truly only one transcription site per cell and whether it remains stable through multiple generations.

Both address the stochastic model application (C41-C43, C49). OpenEval finds the model fits experimental FISH data well with consistent parameters. Peer reviewers identified confusion in model presentation, questioning whether axes and parameters were correctly labeled and whether 'rate' vs 'time' terminology was used appropriately.

Both evaluate photoactivatable ligand characterization (C56-C58, C60). OpenEval finds chemical characterization and antagonist properties well-demonstrated through competition experiments. Peer reviewers questioned the mechanism, asking whether PA exists only transiently due to blocking by excess caged PA and requesting proof of this interpretation.

Both address the temporal delay and chromatin remodeling hypothesis (C80, C83, C86). OpenEval marks mechanistic explanations as explicitly speculative, noting observations are valid but specific molecular events are not directly demonstrated. Peer reviewers directly challenged the interpretation, questioning whether the delay reflects biological chromatin remodeling or reporter system artifacts, and requested testing with endogenous genes.

Both address chromatin-dependent frequency modulation (C52, C66). OpenEval finds the integrated vs episomal comparison provides critical negative controls supporting chromatin's role. Peer reviewers expressed uncertainty about whether observations in this artificial system reflect natural gene regulation, requesting validation with endogenous steroid-regulated genes.

Partial overlap on dose-dependent observations (C46-C48). OpenEval finds these direct experimental measurements well-supported. Peer reviewers raised concerns about cell health (nuclear blebbing, irregular nuclei indicative of apoptosis) and DNA damage from UV exposure, which could alter data interpretation.

Minimal overlap on chromatin remodeling speculation (C85). OpenEval finds literature synthesis reasonable with appropriate caution about speculation. Peer reviewers questioned whether the observed delay reflects biological chromatin remodeling or system complexity, requesting validation with endogenous genes.

OpenEval evaluated mechanistic model claims (C74-C76, C78) as uncertain because they are speculative and not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific mechanistic framework.

OpenEval evaluated background knowledge and prior work claims (C1, C4-C19, C54) as appropriately supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on experimental claims rather than literature context.
